name: CashCowCoin
technique: privileged burn + premature sync() drains PancakeSwap pair

rootCause: privileged burn + premature sync() drains PancakeSwap pair. Lost: ~165.47 WBNB (~$117.4K)

descriptions.text: privileged burn + premature sync() drains PancakeSwap pair. Lost: ~165.47 WBNB (~$117.4K)

CashCowCoin’s unverified trading router implementation contract had a flawed sell() flow. After the PancakeSwap Router completed the CCC→WBNB swap, the proxy called a privileged token function to transfer post-tax CCC from the Pair to the dead address and invoked Pair.sync(). This burned the sell-side CCC while permanently retaining the reduced WBNB reserve, enabling repeated draining of the pool’s WBNB through about 80 iterative sell cycles.

CCC, also referred to as CashCowCoin in secondary coverage, was reported exploited on BNB Chain for about $117,000 after a sell() path burned liquidity-pair tokens and skewed the AMM reserve ratio. The full transaction trace and trigger path were not public in the available record. A swap logic flaw in CCC's sell() path let the token contract alter the liquidity pair's CCC balance and then re-sync around the changed reserve state. The exact trigger path and access-control failure remain unknown from the available evidence.
